claims.text: The ductile-brittle-ductile transition in aged AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is driven by non-monotonic evolution of the L12 ordered-domain fraction coupled to jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a disordered FCC matrix and a B2 intermetallic phase.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 exhibits high ductility and homogeneous deformation.
Aging near 600°C maximizes the L12 ordered-domain fraction in the FCC matrix and brings local chemistry toward the Ni3Al stoichiometric ratio.
High L12 ordering near 600°C raises the antiphase-boundary energy.
The elevated antiphase-boundary energy suppresses dislocation cross-slip.
Suppression of cross-slip forces deformation into planar slip bands.
Planar slip bands terminate at or impinge on jagged B2/FCC interfaces.
Serration teeth at jagged B2/FCC interfaces concentrate stress and, when dislocations cannot cross-slip around them, nucleate cracks and cause brittle fracture.
Aging near 750°C partially disorders the L12 structure and lowers the antiphase-boundary energy.
The lower antiphase-boundary energy after 750°C aging restores cross-slip and ductility.
Aging near 750°C relaxes the interface morphology or creates ductile amorphous-like transition zones along the interfaces.
Aging at 600°C for approximately 10–100 hours is sufficient to reach peak L12 ordering.
Tensile elongation after 600°C aging will be below 5%.
Tensile elongation after 750°C aging will recover to above 20%.
The ductile-to-brittle transition occurs when the L12 ordering fraction exceeds approximately 0.45.
The brittle-to-ductile transition occurs when the L12 ordering fraction falls below approximately 0.30.
Superlattice diffraction contrast or streaking and dislocation dissociation width can be used to estimate the antiphase-boundary energy.
Nanoindentation pop-in statistics can provide a critical resolved shear stress specifically for cross-slip.
Focused-ion-beam milling can flatten the relevant B2/FCC interface while preserving the 600°C ordering state, thereby isolating interface jaggedness from chemical ordering.

contradictions.description: The mechanism explicitly predicts that high ordering and high APBE produce planar slip, independently of whether the interface is jagged. The proposed rule nevertheless treats planar slip in a flattened-interface specimen as falsification. That observation would support the ordering-to-planar-slip link and would only challenge the requirement for jaggedness in fracture initiation.

The mechanism proposes that the interface morphology relaxes at 750°C, whereas the uncertainty statement says the hypothesis assumes jagged morphology is static or evolves more slowly than ordering. The applicable time and temperature range of the static-interface assumption is therefore internally ambiguous.
